statement: Hominin remains at Dmanisi, Georgia (Caucasus), dated 1.85-1.78 million years ago via the associated stratigraphy, represent the earliest confirmed hominin presence outside Africa. The material is anatomically primitive/mosaic, mixing habilis-like and erectus-like traits; the most complete specimen is Dmanisi Skull 5 (D4500), the most complete Early Pleistocene Homo skull known.

sources.citation: Ferring, R., Oms, O., Agústí, J., et al. "Earliest human occupations at Dmanisi (Georgian Caucasus) dated to 1.85-1.78 Ma." PNAS 108(26): 10432-10436.
sources.author: Ferring et al.

does_not_demonstrate: that this was the only or the earliest possible dispersal of hominins out of Africa — it is the earliest currently confirmed by dated fossil evidence
that Dmanisi hominins are taxonomically identical to African Homo erectus populations — a minority position (led by the Dmanisi excavation team) treats them as a distinct taxon, "Homo georgicus"
